allocation: whole scenes by BLAKE2b(scene_id) rank, stratified per naming family

allocation_algorithm.allocation: Whole reconstructed scenes allocated in deterministic order until approximately 20% of trajectories are assigned while preserving naming-family composition.
allocation_algorithm.canonical_input: the scene_key_v1 string, UTF-8 encoded, with no salt or prefix
allocation_algorithm.per_family_application: the 20% trajectory target is applied within each naming family independently, so both partitions retain the corpus's family composition
allocation_algorithm.seed: not applicable -- allocation is a deterministic function of scene_key_v1 via BLAKE2b
allocation_algorithm.sort_rule: ascending lexicographic order of the hex digest

allocation_criterion: held-out trajectory share ~= 20% per naming family; scene counts are a consequence, not a target
inclusion_rationale: Both naming families are INCLUDED. The released checkpoint trained on the entire corpus, so the evaluation population should represent what the historical anchor's referent consumed; excluding a family would move our population further from the anchor's, not closer.

manifest_core_verbatim.allocation: Scene-grouped holdout, stratified across the no* and sim* naming families.
manifest_core_verbatim.grouping_status: Reconstructed scene grouping; no native scene identifier is present in traj_data.pkl.
manifest_core_verbatim.interpretation: The sim* prefix has no verified semantic interpretation. It is not classified as simulation data. Stratification is used only to preserve the observed family composition and make it explicit.
manifest_core_verbatim.leakage_control: No scene_key_v1 value may appear in both development and holdout partitions.
manifest_core_verbatim.scene_key_rule: scene_key_v1 extracts the location code matching ^(no\d+|sim\d+).
manifest_core_verbatim.variant_handling:
Suffixes such as vc, vcF and h are excluded from scene identity.
Trajectories sharing a location code remain in the same scene group.

open_provenance_question: F-M2-3 (UNVERIFIED): the reference corpus contains an undocumented second scene-naming family. Recorded so the population is described rather than assumed. Not a blocker for G0.c.
scene_identity: RECONSTRUCTED -- GO Stanford ships no scene field; traj_data.pkl carries position and yaw only

scene_key_derivation.collision_check: All 3696 names parse; 0 unparsed; no singleton scenes.
scene_key_derivation.native_scene_field: absent -- traj_data.pkl carries only position and yaw
scene_key_derivation.problem: A key retaining the variant suffix yields 106 groups because no2vc and no2vcF are counted separately, which would split one location across train and test.
scene_key_derivation.why_not_scene_of: navfm.splits.scene_of parses at recording level, which would group more finely than location and reintroduce the same leak.
scene_key_derivation.why_the_F_variant_is_the_same_scene: Paired names share suffix sets and trajectory counts exactly (no2vc/no2vcF 175/175, no5vc/no5vcF 122/122, no3vc/no3vcF 76/76). They are NOT duplicates: sampled pairs have genuinely different trajectories (no2vc_101_0 vs no2vcF_101_0, max |dpos| 37.13, max |dyaw| 50.91) and their frames are not mirrors of one another (mean abs pixel difference 64.9; horizontal-flip test negative). They are distinct traversals of one location, so they are one scene and must not be split apart.

stratification_basis: NAMING-FAMILY COMPOSITION PRESERVATION under unresolved provenance. Allocation is stratified by the naming family of the scene key so that both partitions retain the corpus's family composition. This is NOT domain stratification, NOT balancing of any acquisition modality, and is NOT evidence that the families differ in origin. The families are orthographic categories whose meaning is undetermined -- see F-M2-3.
